diagnosis: Customer is on Unified Auth, so credentials are scoped API keys rather than an account-wide token; a suspected leak means rotation is needed, not reset mechanics. KB-0003 covers the correct flow: create a replacement key with the required scopes, cut traffic over, then revoke the old key. Note revocation is immediate with no grace period, so sequencing matters.
reply: Since your account uses Unified Auth, your API credential is managed as a scoped key, and the safe rotation path is: 1) Create a new scoped key with the same scopes as the potentially leaked one (scopes cannot be added to an existing key, so set them at creation). 2) Update your applications to use the new key. 3) Revoke the old key. Please be aware that revocation takes effect immediately with no grace period, so make sure traffic has fully moved to the new key before revoking the old one to avoid downtime. You can find these steps in our knowledge base article on scoped API keys.
